Django: 2.0.5

Without any celery-beat | celery-results.

RC2 works fine.

issue.title: Regression: Apps aren't loaded yet
issue.body:
Worker is broken in rc3 whereas it worked in rc2.

Report is broken in celery >= 4.1 (other versions untested).

The problem seems to be that Django urlconf is loaded too early, which causes some Django import that is too early in the app loading process.

### rc2

Works fine.

Could you all please try this patch: https://github.com/celery/celery/pull/4719

Does this make the worker start again for you?
RC3 + patch https://github.com/celery/celery/pull/4719 works for me (celery worker also celery beat)

Hi, @jonashaag I have the same issue here. 
But I found something weird in my scenario: 
It only happens when I try to import the models to the task.
celery==4.2.1
Django==2.0.1
my celery config is [here](https://github.com/edersonbadeca/kamu/blob/celery-support/kamu/celery.py)
my [tasks file](https://github.com/edersonbadeca/kamu/blob/celery-support/books/tasks.py#L8)

I am using Redis as backend. 

command to reproduce:
api celery -A kamu beat -l debug
if you clone the project and have docker installed:

```docker-compose build
docker-compose run --rm --service-ports api celery -A kamu beat -l debug```

Thanks!!

I have fixed the problem by import the models only in the tasks and allow the auto discover task to find in the whole application instead of installed apps section.

Thank you

Don't use:
```python
from tasks import add
def setup_periodic_tasks(sender, **kwargs):
    # Calls test('hello') every 10 seconds.
    sender.add_periodic_task(10.0, add.s(16,16), name='add every 10')
```

let use:
```python
app.conf.beat_schedule = {
   # Calls test('hello') every 10 seconds.
    'add every 10': {
        'task': 'tasks.add',
        'schedule': 10.0,
        'args': (16, 16)
    },
}
```
You don't need `from tasks import add` which makes error `AppRegistryNotReady`
